memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Nevertheless, some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather it, but
they found none. Then the LORD said to Moses, 'How long will you refuse to keep
my commands and my instructions? Bear in mind that the LORD has given you the
Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Everyone
is to stay where they are on the seventh day; no one is to go out.' So the people
rested on the seventh day." - Ex 16:27-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
They were told there would be nothing. Some went out looking anyway.

It is easy to judge them, but look at the impulse honestly. This is not
rebellion for its own sake. This is anxiety. They could not quite believe the
provision would hold, so they went to check.

Many of us do exactly this. We say we trust God, and then we go out on the
seventh day just to make sure. We take the extra shift, check the balance again,
run the worry through our minds one more time. It is not defiance. It is fear
wearing the clothes of diligence.

Notice what God says: "the LORD has given you the Sabbath." He calls it a gift.
And His question, "How long will you refuse?", is not about a broken rule so
much as a refused gift.

That reframes things. Refusing to rest is not extra devotion. It is quietly
declining something God is holding out to us.

The chapter ends simply: "So the people rested on the seventh day." They learned.
It took a failed attempt, but they learned.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where does your anxiety dress itself up as diligence?
2. What gift from God are you refusing because you cannot quite trust it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for the ways I check and strive instead of trusting. Help me
to receive rest as the gift You intend it to be. Amen.
